records.source: כִּֽי־יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם־לֹ֧א תִמְצָא־חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי־מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: When takes [a] man [a] woman and marries her, and it will be, if not she finds favor in his eyes because he has found in her [the] nakedness of [a] thing, and he writes for her [a] document of cutting off and gives [it] in her hand and sends her from his house,
pieces: Suppose a man marries a woman, but she does not please him because he has found something indecent about her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her and sends her out of his house,

L.1: When a man takes a woman and marries her, and it happens that she does not find favor in his eyes, because he has found in her something indecent, and he writes her a certificate of divorce and puts [it] in her hand and sends her away from his house,

R.1: A man may marry a woman and later decide that he does not want her, because he has found something shameful about her. So he writes out a certificate of divorce, gives it to her and sends her away from his home.

decisions.choice: verses 1-3 set out one case, and verse 4 gives the ruling
decisions.reason: The whole of verses 1-4 is a single case. Verses 1-3 describe what has happened, step by step, and only verse 4 says what is forbidden: the first husband may not take the woman back. The law takes divorce as something that already happens; it does not command it or set its grounds, but limits what may follow. This is still Moses speaking, inside the speech that began at 5:1 and runs to 26:19.

decisions.choice: something indecent: some shameful fault, its exact nature not stated
decisions.reason: The words mean "nakedness of a thing", something exposed that should be covered. The same phrase is used in 23:15 of filth left uncovered in the camp. It is not adultery, which the law punishes by death (22:22). Beyond that the text does not say what is meant, and in Jesus' day Jewish teachers disagreed: some held it meant only serious sexual misconduct, others any fault at all (Matthew 19:3).

decisions.choice: a certificate of divorce: a written document of release, given to the wife
decisions.reason: The words are "a document of cutting off". The husband had to write it and put it in her hand. It ended the marriage formally and gave the woman proof that she was free to marry again, so that she could not be accused of adultery later. Isaiah 50:1 and Jeremiah 3:8 use the same document as a picture of God and his people.

decisions.choice: taken up in Matthew 5:31; 19:7 and Mark 10:4
decisions.reason: When Jesus was asked about divorce, his questioners pointed to this passage: Moses commanded a certificate of divorce. Jesus answered that Moses allowed divorce because of the hardness of people's hearts, but that it was not so from the beginning (Matthew 19:8; Mark 10:5-9; Genesis 2:24).

decisions.choice: she does not find favor in his eyes: she no longer pleases him
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to be pleasing or acceptable to them (Genesis 6:8; Ruth 2:10).

decisions.choice: Suppose a man marries / A man may marry
decisions.reason: Balanced opens with "Suppose", so the long case can run through verses 1-3 before the ruling in verse 4. Readable breaks the case into short sentences. Both say "marry" for the two Hebrew verbs "take" and "become her husband", which Literal keeps.

records.heading: Divorce and remarriage

records.source: וְיָצְאָ֖ה מִבֵּית֑וֹ וְהָלְכָ֖ה וְהָיְתָ֥ה לְאִישׁ־אַחֵֽר׃
records.gloss: and she goes out from his house and goes and becomes [wife] to another man,
pieces: and she leaves his house and becomes the wife of another man,

L.2: and she goes out of his house and goes and becomes another man's [wife],

R.2: She leaves his house and marries another man.

decisions.choice: still part of the case: her second marriage is taken for granted
decisions.reason: The verse goes on with the steps of the case. The divorce has left the woman free, and her marriage to another man is not condemned; the law is concerned only with what happens after it (verse 4).

decisions.choice: becomes to another man: becomes his wife
decisions.reason: "To be to a man" is a common way of saying to be married to him (Ruth 1:12-13).

decisions.choice: wife / marries
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "wife" in brackets; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

records.source: וּשְׂנֵאָהּ֮ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן֒ וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּית֑וֹ א֣וֹ כִ֤י יָמוּת֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָאַחֲר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־לְקָחָ֥הּ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: and hates her the man the latter and writes for her [a] document of cutting off and gives [it] in her hand and sends her from his house, or if dies the man the latter who took her for himself as wife,
pieces: and the second husband turns against her too, writes out a certificate of divorce for her, puts it in her hand and sends her from his house, or if the second husband who married her dies,

L.3: and the latter man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce and puts [it] in her hand and sends her away from his house, or if the latter man who took her to himself as a wife dies,

R.3: Then the second husband may also turn against her, give her a certificate of divorce and send her away. Or the second husband may die.

decisions.choice: hates her: turns against her and no longer wants her as his wife
decisions.reason: In laws about marriage the verb describes a husband who rejects his wife, not necessarily a strong feeling of hatred (21:15-17; 22:13, 16). It is the language of divorce.

decisions.choice: two ways the second marriage may end, with the same result
decisions.reason: The second marriage may end by divorce or by the husband's death. Either way the woman is free again, and verse 4 applies in both cases. So the rule does not depend on how the second marriage ended but on the fact that there was one.

decisions.choice: the second husband
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the latter man"; Balanced and Readable say "the second husband", which is what he is.

records.source: לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל בַּעְלָ֣הּ הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן אֲשֶֽׁר־שִׁ֠לְּחָהּ לָשׁ֨וּב לְקַחְתָּ֜הּ לִהְי֧וֹת ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֗ה אַחֲרֵי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֻטַּמָּ֔אָה כִּֽי־תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תַחֲטִיא֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: not is able her husband the former who sent her away to return to take her to be to him as wife after that she has been made unclean, for [an] abomination it [is] before Yahweh, and not you will cause to sin the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you [as an] inheritance.
pieces: then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back to be his wife, since she has been made unclean. That would be detestable in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You must not bring sin on the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as an inheritance.

L.4: her first husband, who sent her away, is not able to take her again to be his wife after she has been made unclean, for that [is] an abomination before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and you shall not bring sin on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you [as] an inheritance.

R.4: In either case, her first husband, who sent her away, is not allowed to marry her again. She has been made unclean. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} would hate that. Do not bring sin on the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to be your own.

decisions.choice: the ruling: the first husband may not remarry her
decisions.reason: This is the point of the whole case of verses 1-4. The woman is not punished, and her second marriage is not undone; what is forbidden is a return to the first husband. The words "is not able" here mean "is not allowed".

decisions.choice: she has been made unclean: unclean as a wife for the first husband
alternatives: she has been defiled by the second marriage itself
decisions.reason: The verb is a rare passive form, "she has been caused to be unclean". She is not unclean for everyone, since the law lets her marry a second time. The defilement concerns going back: once she has been another man's wife, her return to the first would be treated like adultery. The text does not explain the reason further. Some see the law as a guard against a husband divorcing his wife lightly, or against a man passing a wife to another and taking her back.

decisions.choice: abomination: something the LORD finds detestable
decisions.reason: As in 17:1, the word names what is utterly offensive to God.

decisions.choice: bring sin on the land: make the land guilty
decisions.reason: The verb means "cause to sin". The people's wrongdoing stains the land the LORD gives them (21:23; Leviticus 18:24-28). Jeremiah 3:1 takes up this law: a husband may not return to such a wife, yet the LORD calls unfaithful Israel to return to him.

decisions.choice: detestable / would hate that
decisions.reason: As in 17:1, Literal keeps "abomination", Balanced says "detestable" and Readable says plainly that the LORD would hate it.

decisions.choice: then / In either case
decisions.reason: Balanced begins with "then" to close the "Suppose" of verse 1. Readable, which has told the case in separate sentences, begins with "In either case" to point back to the two endings of verse 3.

records.source: כִּֽי־יִקַּ֥ח אִישׁ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה לֹ֤א יֵצֵא֙ בַּצָּבָ֔א וְלֹא־יַעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֖יו לְכָל־דָּבָ֑ר נָקִ֞י יִהְיֶ֤ה לְבֵיתוֹ֙ שָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְשִׂמַּ֖ח אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־לָקָֽח׃ס
records.gloss: When takes [a] man [a] woman new, not he will go out in the army, and not will pass on him for any thing; free he will be for his house one year, and he will make glad his wife whom he has taken.
pieces: When a man has just married, he is not to go out with the army or have any other duty laid on him. He is to be free to stay at home for a year and give joy to his new wife.

L.5: When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army, and nothing shall be laid on him for any matter; he shall be free for his house one year, and he shall make glad his wife whom he has taken.

R.5: A man who has just married must not be sent to war, and he must not be given any other work for the community either. For one year he is free to stay home and make his new wife happy.

decisions.choice: takes a new wife: marries for the first time with this woman
decisions.reason: "Takes a woman" means marries. "New" describes the marriage as just made, not a second wife added to a first.

decisions.choice: nothing shall pass on him: no public duty is to be put on him
decisions.reason: The words mean that no task or levy is to "pass over" onto him. Besides war, this covers other service for the people, such as forced labor or other public work.

decisions.choice: make glad his wife: give her joy
decisions.reason: The vowels of the text read the verb as "make glad": the year is for the wife's sake. The same letters could be read "rejoice with his wife". Either way the year is given to the new marriage.

decisions.choice: compare 20:7
decisions.reason: In 20:7 a man who is engaged but not yet married is sent home from battle. This law goes further, keeping a newly married man at home for a whole year.

decisions.choice: free to stay at home / free to stay home
decisions.reason: "Free for his house" means free of duty so that he can be at home. Balanced and Readable say so. Readable adds "for the community" to make clear what kind of other work is meant (m2).

records.source: לֹא־יַחֲבֹ֥ל רֵחַ֖יִם וָרָ֑כֶב כִּי־נֶ֖פֶשׁ ה֥וּא חֹבֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: Not one will take in pledge [a] hand-mill or [an] upper millstone, for [a] life he [is] taking in pledge.
pieces: Do not take a hand mill, or even its upper millstone, in pledge for a debt. That would be taking in pledge the very means a person lives by.

L.6: One shall not take in pledge a hand mill or an upper millstone, for he is taking a life in pledge.

R.6: Do not take someone's grinding stones, not even the top one, to hold until a loan is paid back. People need them to make food. Taking them is like taking a person's life.

decisions.choice: a hand mill or an upper millstone: the two stones used to grind grain at home
decisions.reason: The first word names the pair of stones of a hand mill. The second, "rider", is the smaller upper stone, rubbed back and forth over the lower one. Flour was ground every day for the day's bread, so a household without its mill, or even without the upper stone, could not eat.

decisions.choice: take in pledge: hold something of the borrower's until a loan is repaid
decisions.reason: A lender could keep an object belonging to the borrower as a guarantee. This law and verses 10-13 and 17 limit what may be taken and how.

decisions.choice: taking a life in pledge: taking what the borrower needs to stay alive
decisions.reason: The word "life" here stands for what keeps a person alive. To hold the mill is to hold the family's living.

decisions.choice: People need them to make food.
decisions.reason: Readable explains why the stones matter, from m1, so the reason at the end can be understood.

records.source: כִּי־יִמָּצֵ֣א אִ֗ישׁ גֹּנֵ֨ב נֶ֤פֶשׁ מֵאֶחָיו֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִתְעַמֶּר־בּ֖וֹ וּמְכָר֑וֹ וּמֵת֙ הַגַּנָּ֣ב הַה֔וּא וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: If is found [a] man stealing [a] person from his brothers, from [the] sons of Israel, and he treats him as a slave and sells him, and will die the thief that, and you will purge the evil from your midst.
pieces: If anyone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating the victim as a slave or selling him, that kidnapper must die. You must purge the evil from among you.

L.7: If {{gender:someone|a man}} is found stealing a person from among his brothers, from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and treats him as a slave and sells him, then that thief shall die; so you shall purge the evil from your midst.

R.7: Someone may kidnap a fellow Israelite and then make that person a slave or sell them. If the kidnapper is caught, the kidnapper must die. You must get rid of this evil among you.

decisions.choice: stealing a person: kidnapping
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word for stealing, here with a person as its object. Exodus 21:16 gives the same penalty for kidnapping. "Is found" means caught and proved guilty.

decisions.choice: treats him as a slave: deals with him as property
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; it is found only here and in 21:14, where a man may not treat a captive woman this way. It seems to mean to treat someone as goods to use or trade, or to deal with them by force. The exact shade is not certain.

decisions.choice: and ... and: either act completes the crime
decisions.reason: The word "and" links two ways of making use of the stolen person. Exodus 21:16 makes the kidnapper guilty whether he has sold the person or still holds him, so either is enough.

decisions.choice: purge the evil from your midst: remove the wrong and the wrongdoer
decisions.reason: As in 13:6 and 17:7, this saying closes a law that carries the death penalty.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "slave", because the law is about a person seized and sold as property, where the style guide keeps the word.

decisions.choice: someone / anyone; fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: The law covers any kidnapper and any Israelite victim. Literal offers "someone" by default and keeps "his brothers"; Balanced and Readable say "anyone" and "a fellow Israelite" for "one of his brothers, the sons of Israel".

records.source: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר בְּנֶֽגַע־הַצָּרַ֛עַת לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְאֹ֖ד וְלַעֲשׂ֑וֹת כְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר־יוֹר֨וּ אֶתְכֶ֜ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים הַלְוִיִּ֛ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖ם תִּשְׁמְר֥וּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: Guard yourself in [the] mark of the scale disease, to keep very much and to do according to all which will teach you the priests the Levites; just as I commanded them, you will keep to do.
pieces: When a serious skin disease breaks out, take great care to do exactly what the Levitical priests teach you. Be careful to follow what I commanded them.

L.8: Be on guard in a mark of scale disease, to be very careful and to do according to all that the priests, the Levites, teach you; as I commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.

R.8: If someone gets a serious skin disease, be very careful to do everything the priests from the tribe of Levi tell you. Do exactly what I commanded them.

decisions.choice: scale disease: a group of skin conditions that made a person unclean
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 13-14, the word covers a range of skin diseases, and also mold in cloth and houses. It is not modern leprosy. A priest had to examine the person, and the one found unclean had to live outside the camp until healed (Leviticus 13:46).

decisions.choice: mark: an outbreak or patch of disease
decisions.reason: The word means a "touch" or "stroke", and so a mark of disease on the skin, as in Leviticus 13:2-3.

decisions.choice: as I commanded them: the priests teach the rules already given
decisions.reason: The detailed rules were given to Moses and Aaron (Leviticus 13:1; 14:1). The priests are to teach them and the people are to follow their ruling (17:9-11; 33:10). The command first speaks to Israel as one person, then turns to the plural "you" in its second half.

decisions.choice: serious skin disease; Levitical priests / priests from the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "scale disease" and "the priests, the Levites"; Balanced and Readable say "serious skin disease", as in Leviticus 13, and Balanced "Levitical priests", as in 17:9.

records.source: זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְמִרְיָ֑ם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: Remember what did Yahweh your God to Miriam on the way when you came out from Egypt.
pieces: Remember what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to Miriam on your journey after you came out of Egypt.

L.9: Remember what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.

R.9: Remember what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to Miriam while you were traveling after you left Egypt. He made her sick with this skin disease.

decisions.choice: what the LORD did to Miriam: Numbers 12
decisions.reason: When Miriam spoke against Moses, the LORD struck her with scale disease, and she had to be shut outside the camp for seven days before she could come back (Numbers 12:10-15). Not even Moses' sister was spared the rules for the disease, and it came on her as a judgment.

decisions.choice: remember: the reason for verse 8
decisions.reason: The reminder backs up the command to follow the priests' teaching. The form of the verb gives it emphasis, as in 25:17.

decisions.choice: He made her sick with this skin disease.
decisions.reason: Readable says what the LORD did, from Numbers 12:10, since a reader may not know the story.

records.source: כִּֽי־תַשֶּׁ֥ה בְרֵֽעֲךָמַשַּׁ֣את מְא֑וּמָה לֹא־תָבֹ֥א אֶל־בֵּית֖וֹ לַעֲבֹ֥ט עֲבֹטֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: When you lend to your neighbor [a] loan of anything, not you will go into his house to take as pledge his pledge.
pieces: When you lend your neighbor anything, do not go into his house to pick out what he will give you as security.

L.10: When you make your neighbor a loan of any kind, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.

R.10: When you lend something to a neighbor, do not go into that neighbor's house to take something to keep until the loan is paid back.

decisions.choice: his pledge: an object the borrower hands over as a guarantee
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the lender may hold something of the borrower's until the loan is repaid. The law does not forbid the pledge; it forbids the lender to enter the house and choose it himself.

decisions.choice: do not go into his house: the borrower keeps his dignity
decisions.reason: A man's house is his own, even when he is in debt. He, not the lender, decides what to hand over, and he brings it out himself (verse 11). The law protects the weaker party, as Exodus 22:24-26 does.

decisions.choice: lend ... a loan: lend against a pledge
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from the same root, which is used of loans given on security (15:2).

decisions.choice: pick out what he will give you as security / take something to keep
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "take his pledge". Balanced and Readable say what a pledge is, and Balanced says "pick out" to bring out the point that the choice is the borrower's (m2).

records.heading: Pledges and wages

records.source: בַּח֖וּץ תַּעֲמֹ֑ד וְהָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ נֹשֶׁ֣ה ב֔וֹ יוֹצִ֥יא אֵלֶ֛יךָ אֶֽת־הַעֲב֖וֹט הַחֽוּצָה׃
records.gloss: Outside you will stand, and the man who you [are] lending to him will bring out to you the pledge outside.
pieces: Wait outside, and let the borrower bring the pledge out to you.

L.11: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you are lending shall bring the pledge out to you, outside.

R.11: Stay outside, and let the person who is borrowing bring it out to you.

decisions.choice: outside ... outside: the word is repeated for stress
decisions.reason: The verse begins and ends with "outside". The lender stays at the door and the exchange happens there.

decisions.choice: the borrower / the person who is borrowing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the man by what he is doing, for "the man to whom you are lending". Balanced leaves out the second "outside", which in a shorter sentence repeats nothing new.

records.source: וְאִם־אִ֥ישׁ עָנִ֖י ה֑וּא לֹ֥א תִשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּעֲבֹטֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if [a] man poor he [is], not you will lie down in his pledge.
pieces: If he is poor, do not go to bed with his pledge still in your keeping.

L.12: And if he [is] a poor man, you shall not lie down in his pledge.

R.12: If the borrower is poor and gives you his coat, do not keep it overnight.

decisions.choice: lie down in his pledge: keep the pledge through the night
decisions.reason: The words may picture the lender sleeping wrapped in the poor man's cloak, or simply going to bed while still holding it. Either way the pledge must not stay with the lender overnight (verse 13).

decisions.choice: a poor man: one who has nothing else to give
decisions.reason: A poor man's only pledge might be his cloak, the outer garment he also slept in (verse 13; Exodus 22:25-26).

decisions.choice: and gives you his coat
decisions.reason: Readable names the pledge from verse 13, so that "keep it overnight" is clear.

records.source: הָשֵׁב֩ תָּשִׁ֨יב ל֤וֹ אֶֽת־הַעֲבוֹט֙ כְּבֹ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וְשָׁכַ֥ב בְּשַׂלְמָת֖וֹ וּבֵֽרֲכֶ֑ךָּ וּלְךָ֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה צְדָקָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ס
records.gloss: Surely you will return to him the pledge at [the] going of the sun, and he will lie down in his cloak and he will bless you, and to you it will be righteousness before Yahweh your God.
pieces: Be sure to give the pledge back to him at sunset, so that he can sleep in his cloak and bless you. It will be counted as righteousness for you in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.13: You shall surely return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, and he shall lie down in his cloak and bless you; and it shall be righteousness for you before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.13: Be sure to give it back to him before the sun goes down. Then he can sleep in his coat, and he will bless you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will count this as a righteous act.

decisions.choice: his cloak: the outer garment, used as a blanket at night
decisions.reason: The poor had no other covering for the cold nights (Exodus 22:25-26). So the lender may take it during the day but must give it back each evening.

decisions.choice: surely return: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to make the command strong: the pledge must certainly come back.

decisions.choice: righteousness before the LORD: an act God recognizes as right
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 6:25. Kindness to the poor borrower is counted by God as doing what is right in his covenant. The poor man's blessing stands against his cry against the lender in verse 15.

decisions.choice: he will bless you: he will ask God's good for you
decisions.reason: The poor man calls down God's blessing on the lender who treats him well. Job 29:13 and 31:20 speak of the same blessing from the poor.

decisions.choice: will count this as a righteous act
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word but turns "it will be righteousness for you" into a simpler sentence with the LORD as subject, as 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: cloak / coat
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "cloak"; Readable says "coat", a plainer word for the outer garment.

records.source: לֹא־תַעֲשֹׁ֥ק שָׂכִ֖יר עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן מֵאַחֶ֕יךָ א֧וֹ מִגֵּרְךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאַרְצְךָ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Not you will oppress [a] hired worker poor and needy, from your brothers or from your sojourner who [is] in your land in your gates.
pieces: Do not take advantage of a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether a fellow Israelite or an outsider living in one of the towns of your land.

L.14: You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether one of your brothers or one of your sojourners who [are] in your land, within your gates.

R.14: Do not cheat a poor worker you have hired, someone who is in need. It does not matter if the worker is a fellow Israelite or an outsider who lives in one of your towns.

decisions.choice: oppress: exploit, hold back what is due
decisions.reason: The verb means to wrong someone by abusing power over them, especially by keeping back their pay (Leviticus 19:13; Malachi 3:5). Verse 15 shows the case in mind.

decisions.choice: a hired worker: a laborer paid by the day
decisions.reason: Such a worker had no land of his own and lived on his daily wage. He was free, not owned, but he depended on the one who hired him.

decisions.choice: your brothers or your sojourner: the same protection for both
decisions.reason: The law does not let an outsider be treated worse than an Israelite. As in 10:18-19, God cares for the sojourner, and so must Israel.

decisions.choice: within your gates: in your towns
decisions.reason: As in 15:7, "your gates" means the towns where Israel lives.

decisions.choice: fellow Israelite; outsider
decisions.reason: As in 15:7 and 16:11, Balanced and Readable say "fellow Israelite" for "your brothers" and "outsider" for the sojourner. Readable says "cheat" for "oppress", the form the wrong takes here (m1).

records.source: בְּיוֹמוֹ֩ תִתֵּ֨ן שְׂכָר֜וֹ וְֽלֹא־תָב֧וֹא עָלָ֣יו הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י עָנִי֙ ה֔וּא וְאֵלָ֕יו ה֥וּא נֹשֵׂ֖א אֶת־נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִקְרָ֤א עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא׃ס
records.gloss: On his day you will give his wage, and not will go on it the sun, for poor he [is], and to it he [is] lifting his soul; and not he will call against you to Yahweh, and it will be in you sin.
pieces: Give him his pay on the day he works, before the sun sets, because he is poor and is counting on it. Otherwise he may call on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} against you, and the sin will be counted against you.

L.15: On his day you shall give him his wage, and the sun shall not go down on it, for he [is] poor and he lifts up his soul to it; so that he does not call out against you to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and there is sin in you.

R.15: Pay the worker at the end of each day, before sunset. The worker is poor and needs that money to live. If you do not, the worker may cry out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about you, and you will be to blame for that sin.

decisions.choice: on his day, before sunset: on the same day the work is done
decisions.reason: The wage must be paid the day it is earned, before night. Leviticus 19:13 forbids keeping a hired worker's wage overnight.

decisions.choice: lifts up his soul to it: sets his heart on it, depends on it
decisions.reason: To lift up one's soul to something is to long for it and rely on it (Psalm 25:1; Jeremiah 22:27). The poor worker needs the day's wage to buy the day's food.

decisions.choice: he calls out against you to the LORD: God hears the cry of the wronged
decisions.reason: As in 15:9 and Exodus 22:22, 26, the LORD hears the cry of the poor. James 5:4 takes up the same picture: the wages held back from the workers cry out, and the Lord hears.

decisions.choice: it will be sin in you: the guilt rests on you
decisions.reason: As in 15:9, the delay is not only unkind; it is sin, and the guilt is counted against the employer.

decisions.choice: is counting on it / needs that money to live
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2). Readable says "If you do not" for the Hebrew "and not", which here gives the reason for the command.

records.source: לֹֽא־יוּמְת֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ עַל־בָּנִ֔ים וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־יוּמְת֣וּ עַל־אָב֑וֹת אִ֥ישבְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יוּמָֽתוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Not will be put to death fathers on account of sons, and sons not will be put to death on account of fathers; [each] man for his sin they will be put to death.
pieces: {{gender:Parents|Fathers}} are not to be put to death for their {{gender:children|sons}}, nor {{gender:children|sons}} for their {{gender:parents|fathers}}. Each one is to be put to death only for {{gender:their|his}} own sin.

L.16: {{gender:Parents|Fathers}} shall not be put to death for {{gender:children|sons}}, and {{gender:children|sons}} shall not be put to death for {{gender:parents|fathers}}; each shall be put to death for {{gender:their|his}} own sin.

R.16: Do not put {{gender:parents|fathers}} to death for what their {{gender:children|sons}} have done. Do not put {{gender:children|sons}} to death for what their {{gender:parents|fathers}} have done. People may be put to death only for their own sin.

decisions.choice: each for his own sin: a court may punish only the guilty person
decisions.reason: The law forbids putting a family member to death in place of the guilty one, or alongside him. Exodus 20:5 and 5:9 speak of God visiting the sin of fathers on children; that describes God's own dealings with those who hate him, while this law binds human judges.

decisions.choice: quoted in 2 Kings 14:6 and 2 Chronicles 25:4
decisions.reason: When King Amaziah executed the officials who had murdered his father, he did not kill their sons, "as it is written in the book of the law of Moses", and the verse is quoted. Jeremiah 31:29-30 and Ezekiel 18:20 build on the same principle.

decisions.choice: fathers ... sons: parents and children
decisions.reason: In a law like this the words cover parents and children of either sex.

decisions.choice: Parents / children; their
decisions.reason: The gender setting gives "parents", "children" and "their" by default and "fathers", "sons" and "his" as the alternative (m3). Readable says "people" for "each man".

records.source: לֹ֣א תַטֶּ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט גֵּ֣ר יָת֑וֹם וְלֹ֣א תַחֲבֹ֔ל בֶּ֖גֶד אַלְמָנָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not you will turn aside [the] justice of [a] sojourner [or a] fatherless [one], and not you will take in pledge [the] garment of [a] widow.
pieces: Do not deny justice to the outsider or the fatherless child, and do not take a widow's cloak in pledge.

L.17: You shall not turn aside the justice of the sojourner [or] the fatherless, and you shall not take a widow's garment in pledge.

R.17: Make sure that outsiders and children without fathers are treated fairly. Do not take a widow's clothing to hold until she pays back a loan.

decisions.choice: turn aside justice: bend a judgment, deny someone their rights
decisions.reason: The same words appear in 16:19 and Exodus 23:6. Those without family to speak for them were easy to wrong in court, and 27:19 puts a curse on anyone who does it.

decisions.choice: the sojourner, the fatherless, the widow: those with no protector
decisions.reason: As in 14:29 and 16:11, these three had no land or no man to provide for them, and God takes up their cause (10:18).

decisions.choice: a widow's garment: not to be taken in pledge at all
decisions.reason: From the poor man the cloak may be taken by day if it is returned at night (verses 12-13). From a widow it may not be taken even for a day.

decisions.choice: outsider; fatherless child / children without fathers
decisions.reason: As in 14:29 and 16:11. Readable states the command positively: "make sure ... are treated fairly" for "do not turn aside the justice of".

records.heading: The outsider, the fatherless and the widow

records.source: וְזָכַרְתָּ֗ כִּ֣י עֶ֤בֶד הָיִ֨יתָ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִשָּׁ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And you will remember that [a] slave you were in Egypt, and redeemed you Yahweh your God from there; therefore I [am] commanding you to do the thing this.
pieces: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

L.18: And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

R.18: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God set you free from there. That is why I am commanding you to do this.

decisions.choice: remember that you were a slave: the reason for the laws of verses 17-18
decisions.reason: Israel knows from its own past what it is to be powerless. As in 15:15 and 16:12, the memory of Egypt is the ground for fairness to the weak.

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free, as a slave is bought out of slavery
decisions.reason: The verb is used of buying back a person or property. The LORD freed Israel from slavery in Egypt (7:8; 15:15).

decisions.choice: slave; slaves
decisions.reason: As in 16:12, every level keeps "slave", because Israel's slavery in Egypt is the point. Balanced and Readable use the plural for the singular that addresses Israel as one person. Readable says "set you free" for "redeemed" (m2).

records.source: כִּ֣י תִקְצֹר֩ קְצִֽירְךָ֨ בְשָׂדֶ֜ךָ וְשָֽׁכַחְתָּ֧ עֹ֣מֶר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה לֹ֤א תָשׁוּב֙ לְקַחְתּ֔וֹ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֑ה לְמַ֤עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: When you harvest your harvest in your field and forget [a] sheaf in the field, not you will return to take it; for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow it will be, so that will bless you Yahweh your God in all [the] work of your hands.
pieces: When you are harvesting your field and leave a sheaf behind by mistake, do not go back for it. Let it go to the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow. That way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless all the work of your hands.

L.19: When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it; it shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

R.19: When you harvest the grain in your field, you may forget a bundle of grain there. Do not go back to get it. Leave it for outsiders, for children without fathers, and for widows. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in all the work you do.

decisions.choice: a sheaf: a bundle of cut grain stalks
decisions.reason: Reapers cut the grain and bound it into sheaves, which were carried to the threshing floor. One left behind in the field is to stay there.

decisions.choice: compare Leviticus 19:9-10; 23:22 and Ruth 2
decisions.reason: Leviticus also tells farmers to leave the edges of the field and the fallen grain. Ruth the widow gathered grain in Boaz's field under these laws (Ruth 2:2-3, 15-16).

decisions.choice: so that the LORD may bless you: generosity and blessing go together
decisions.reason: As in 14:29 and 15:10, what is left for the poor is not lost; God promises to bless the work of those who share.

decisions.choice: bundle of grain; outsider; fatherless child / children without fathers
decisions.reason: Readable says "bundle of grain" for "sheaf". For the three groups, as in 16:11.

records.source: כִּ֤י תַחְבֹּט֙ זֵֽיתְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְפָאֵ֖ר אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶֽה׃ס
records.gloss: When you beat your olive tree, not you will go over the branches after you; for the sojourner, for the fatherless and for the widow it will be.
pieces: When you knock the olives from your trees, do not go back over the branches a second time. What is left is for the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow.

L.20: When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the branches after yourself; it shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

R.20: When you knock down the olives from your trees, do not go back for the ones still on the branches. Leave them for outsiders, for children without fathers, and for widows.

decisions.choice: beat your olive tree: the olives were knocked down with sticks
decisions.reason: Olives were harvested by beating the branches with poles, so that the fruit fell to the ground. Some always stayed on the tree (Isaiah 17:6; 24:13).

decisions.choice: go over the branches after yourself: search the tree a second time
decisions.reason: The verb is related to a word for branches. It means to go back over the boughs for what the first beating missed.

decisions.choice: outsider; fatherless child / children without fathers
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

records.source: כִּ֤י תִבְצֹר֙ כַּרְמְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְעוֹלֵ֖ל אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: When you gather grapes [of] your vineyard, not you will glean after you; for the sojourner, for the fatherless and for the widow it will be.
pieces: When you pick the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over it again for what remains. That is for the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow.

L.21: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean after yourself; it shall be for the sojourner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

R.21: When you pick the grapes in your vineyard, do not go back for the ones you missed. Leave them for outsiders, for children without fathers, and for widows.

decisions.choice: glean: pick the small bunches left after the harvest
decisions.reason: The verb means to gather what remains after the main picking, the small or late clusters. Leviticus 19:10 gives the same rule for the vineyard.

decisions.choice: outsider; fatherless child / children without fathers
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

records.source: וְזָ֣כַרְתָּ֔ כִּי־עֶ֥בֶד הָיִ֖יתָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And you will remember that [a] slave you were in [the] land of Egypt; therefore I [am] commanding you to do the thing this.
pieces: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.

L.22: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

R.22: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. That is why I am commanding you to do this.

decisions.choice: remember that you were a slave: the reason for the harvest laws
decisions.reason: As in verse 18. Israel, once without land or rights in Egypt, must leave part of its harvest for those who have none.

decisions.choice: I am commanding you: still Moses speaking
decisions.reason: The chapter ends inside Moses' long speech of 5:1-26:19, which goes on into chapter 25.

decisions.choice: slave; slaves
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.
